note: SYNTHETIC development cases, defined but never run. One attempt per case, without repair or fallback. Automatic screens are heuristics; human reading decides success. Structural validity does not establish semantic support. These cases' results are not the K6 measurement. The runner differs from production: one attempt with no schema repair, no rate-limit retry, no fallback and exact requested-model equality, synthetic fixture variants rather than database-planned inputs, CB06's three abstracts of one work although the production selector chooses at most one, and neither the production 48,000-character message limit nor the research's chosen reasoning effort is applied.

cases.title: Same result in other terminology
cases.fixture_change: Replace the shown abstract with SYNTHETIC text describing the same buffering mechanism, bounded arrivals and reduced delay using different terminology.
cases.expected: explicit_support with aligned conditions for the stated elements; different terminology alone does not lower the relation.
cases.failure_if: Treats terminology differences alone as partial_match or no_match_in_supplied_text.
cases.builder_note: Only the abstract text changes; the title and the selected-sections distractor stay as in the fixture.
observed_questions: Does other terminology receive explicit support for all three elements?
Are the supported cells aligned with the claim's conditions?

cases.title: Work says nothing about the claim
cases.fixture_change: Replace the title and all passages with SYNTHETIC discussion of wall pigments that says nothing about queues or delay.
cases.expected: unrelated, all cells no_match_in_supplied_text, states_whole_claim false. Zero-result, all-queries-failed and no-abstract states are code states checked in K3 tests, not model behavior; no-abstract with no usable stored passage is not sent to this task.
cases.failure_if: Invents support or declares absence of prior work, novelty or a research gap.
cases.builder_note: The title and both passage texts describe pigments; the abstract and selected-sections shapes stay as in the fixture.
observed_questions: Does the output keep a lack of match in this text separate from absence of prior work?

cases.title: Only one element of a compound claim matches
cases.fixture_change: Show SYNTHETIC text stating buffering alone, with no bounded-arrival condition and no delay result.
cases.expected: related, one supported element with a located quote and the remaining cells no_match_in_supplied_text or uncertain as the text warrants; states_whole_claim false.
cases.failure_if: Transfers one element's support to the rest or sets states_whole_claim true.
cases.builder_note: Only the abstract text changes; the title and the selected-sections distractor stay as in the fixture.
observed_questions: Is support confined to the mechanism?
Does the quote state storage before processing?

cases.title: Attractive but invalid analogy
cases.fixture_change: Use SYNTHETIC passages about biological storage as an attractive analogy, with no statement of the queue mechanism.
cases.expected: Does not treat the analogy in another setting as explicit_support for the claim; describes the supplied text's limits.
cases.failure_if: Calls the analogy a matching mechanism or infers that the work states the whole claim.
cases.builder_note: Both passage texts describe biological storage; the abstract and selected-sections shapes and source title stay as in the fixture.
observed_questions: Does the output call the analogy a matching mechanism?
How many cells use reasoned_inference, and what justifies each?
Does the output infer the whole claim from biological storage?

cases.title: Opposite result under different conditions
cases.fixture_change: Show SYNTHETIC buffering that increases delay under unbounded bursts, instead of the version's bounded arrivals.
cases.expected: Records different_conditions for supported mechanism cells and describes the opposite result under those conditions; never a plain contradiction or a match under the claim's conditions.
cases.failure_if: Sets aligned for the changed conditions or presents the opposite result as a plain contradiction.
cases.builder_note: Only the abstract text changes; it says unbounded bursts, and the selected-sections distractor stays as in the fixture.
observed_questions: Does the output name the changed conditions when discussing the opposite result?

cases.title: Elements stated separately
cases.fixture_change: Make all supplied SYNTHETIC passages abstract passages. State buffering, bounded arrivals and reduced delay in separate settings, never holding together.
cases.expected: May support individual elements but states_whole_claim false and whole_claim_evidence empty; separate statements do not state the compound claim.
cases.failure_if: Sets states_whole_claim true from separately stated parts.
cases.builder_note: Three abstracts of one work are accepted by check_step_input; the third passage and its allowlist entry are added, and the second passage is converted to abstract. Production shown_passages selects at most one abstract per work.
observed_questions: Does any passage state the elements holding together?
Does the output join statements from separate settings into a whole-claim finding?

cases.title: Owner sentence with empty basis
cases.fixture_change: Use the SYNTHETIC owner's sentence with empty basis, sources and passages; keep origin owner_text.
cases.expected: One formulation, nearest_simple_explanation null, empty source_ids and passage_ids; frames the sentence as the owner's proposal, with no literature-supported finding.
cases.failure_if: Invents a nearest explanation or source evidence, improves the idea, or frames it as established by literature.
cases.builder_note: The owner-text fixture changes only in step ids, model and loaded skill_package_hash; basis, sources and passages stay empty.
observed_questions: Does the rationale frame the sentence as the owner's proposal?
does the output improve, strengthen or add a mechanism to the owner's idea?
